subject: biology-1
question: The protein **p53**, a **tumor suppressor**, detects DNA damage and halts the cell cycle at the G1 checkpoint so repair can occur. A cell loses both working copies of the p53 gene. Which outcome is most likely?

options.text: The cell immediately stops dividing and dies.
The cell repairs damaged DNA even more efficiently.
The cell replicates DNA only during G2 instead of S phase.
Damaged DNA no longer triggers a G1 arrest, so mutations accumulate as the cell keeps dividing.

explanation: p53 is a tumor suppressor that enforces G1 arrest when DNA is damaged, so losing it lets damaged cells keep dividing and pile up mutations, a hallmark of cancer. A is wrong because division continues unchecked, B reverses p53's role, and C misplaces DNA replication in G2.
